name: Meiga, Cartuxeira
body:
Cartuxeira
CR 5

This elderly woman is dressed in colorful, flowing skirts and scarves. Her keen eyes gleam with hawkish intensity.

XP 1,600
N Medium fey (extraplanar)
Init +7; Senses darkvision 60 ft., low-light vision; Perception +14

DEFENSE

AC 18, touch 18, flat-footed 14 (+3 Dex, +1 dodge, +4 Wis)
hp 52 (8d6+24)
Fort +5, Ref +9, Will +10
Defensive Abilities improved evasion; DR 10/cold iron; Immune mind-affecting, sleep; SR 16

OFFENSE

Speed 30 ft.
Melee mwk short sword +8 (1d6/19–20 plus 3d6 force)
Ranged mwk dart +8 (1d4 plus 3d6 force)
Special Attacks alter past or future, vision of myriad paths
Spell-Like Abilities (CL 8th; concentration +11)

At will—augury, guidance
3/day—anticipate peril (DC 14), mirror image
1/day—dimension door, divination, dream

STATISTICS

Str 10, Dex 17, Con 16, Int 13, Wis 19, Cha 16
Base Atk +4; CMB +4; CMD 22
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative, Mobility, Weapon Finesse
Skills Acrobatics +13, Bluff +13, Escape Artist +13, Heal +11, Knowledge (arcana) +8, Perception +14, Sense Motive +14, Stealth +13
Languages Common, Sylvan; telepathy 30 ft.
Gear mwk dart, mwk shortsword

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Alter Past or Future (Su)

Once per day as a standard action, a cartuxeira can reach out along the threads of fate, altering an event in the past or future of one creature she can see. The save DCs are Charisma-based.

By manipulating the past, the cartuxeira can add or remove one of the following conditions to the target: blinded, deafened, fatigued, frightened (1d6 rounds), paralyzed (1d6 rounds), sickened (1d6 minutes), or stunned (1 round). She can instead inflict 4d8 points of damage or heal 4d8 hit points. The creature must succeed at a DC 17 Will save to avoid the condition or take half damage.

By manipulating the future, the cartuxeira can change the outcome of one die roll from a success to a failure, or vice versa.

The GM chooses when this occurs. The target must succeed at a DC 17 Will save to avoid this fate manipulation. If the target fails its save, it knows when the fated event has come to pass.

Vision of Myriad Paths (Su)

Once every 1d4 rounds as a standard action, a cartuxeira can choose a target within 60 feet that she can see, perplexing the target’s mind with a flood of various possibilities arising from the next decision it makes. The target must succeed at a DC 17 Will save or become confused until the end of its next turn. The save DC is Charisma-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any land
Organization solitary, pair, or troupe (3-6)
Treasure standard

The cartuxeira is the agent of dreams that predict the future.

She rattles a handful of divinatory tokens and studying their surroundings with bright, wise eyes. Cartuxeiras have has divinatory powers, using bones, cards, runestones, tea leaves, or other instruments, as per her individual preferences. Able to view both the past and the future, the cartuxeria’s greatest power is to reach along those threads of fate and tweak them, altering events or ensuring future events have a different outcome. While this ability has proven combat ability, its usefulness reaches far beyond that. The GM should consider the far-telling effects on a character or campaign should a cartuxeira change an element of the past or future, and its immediate or eventual consequences.

Meigas come from the Land of Dreams, where mortal minds wander while they sleep and use the substance of the land to build the dreams that run through their heads while they slumber. The Land of Dreams is said to be part of the fey realms, but can only be entered through dreaming, except by the most powerful of creatures, or by the fey that dwell there, including the meiga.

Meigas differ widely in form and ability, but always appear as female. Clothing preference varies by individual, but meigas typically prefer bright colors and bold patterns.

While all meiga can magically change their form to blend with mortal populations, their apparent age always shows through. If a meiga’s true appearance is elderly, then she appears elderly in any form she takes, while a more maiden-like meiga is always youthful when magically disguised.

A meiga’s weapons are formed of dream-stuff and have a link to the Land of Dreams. When mortals are hit with such weapons, the pain is increased as their mind relives past pains from memory, brought forth by the meiga’s control over dreams.

While in their own realm, a meiga serves a particular function in maintaining the dreamscapes of mortals. The cartuxeira oversees premonitory dreams of future events.

The lobismuller is the bringer of nightmares. The vedoira are caretakers of dreams in which the spirits of the dead make contact with the living; their purview over dream communication means they are also overseers of those who are contacted via the dream spell. Other types of meigas do exist, exerting their particular influence over the dreams of mortals according to their sphere of influence.

In the Land of Dreams, meigas are typically not hostile, unless waking mortals come and interfere with their duties or disrupt the dreaming of sleepers. However, spellcasters aware of their existence and the powers available to them in the waking world often summon meigas (through spells such as conjure fey) to do their bidding. Such summoners should take great care not to lose control over a meiga, however, as they hold a grudge and will pursue vengeance against those foolish enough to let their mastery of the meiga slip.

Rare Meigasrare Meigas

While the meigas described in this book are the most common and best-known of their kind, other meiga dream-spirits can be encountered more rarely. Their abilities are generally a mystery and they are known by their particular behavior.

Chuchonas. The most dangerous of all meigas, chuchonas appear with different faces or transformed into fanged vampires, but also can take the form of insects, most often bumblebees. They suck the blood of children, especially newborns, to steal their life essence to craft their ointments and potions.
Feiticeira. These meigas live near rivers and streams, appearing as elderly women who still retain their loveliness. The feiticeira has a very beautiful voice that with her singing hypnotizes men and boys who approach the river and makes them go into the river, where they will drown to be later devoured.
Lavandeira. These meigas surprise walkers who passes by a lavandeira (laundry house), inviting him to help her in the same direction as her, because otherwise, misfortune will befall his house. The Lavandeira will appear in the person’s house and will end the pregnancy if there is one, steal the youngest of the children if there are any, or kill one of the spouses while they are sleeping, if there are no children at home.
Marimanta. The origin of these meigas is unknown, but they can be invoked with complex rituals that draw them across both spatial and planar boundaries. They often wanders of their own free will between Dreamland and our world, entering houses where there is a child on which no blessings or protection have been used, and often abducts them to a place from which they never return for reasons and uses unknown to anyone.
